01 / The role

Design information.
A visual conversation.

My internship work at The Laurel Group focused on landscape visualization and the workflows behind it: developing concept images, comparing options, and organizing the steps used to present a design direction.

Site references and design plans provide a starting point. Photoshop compositing and AI-assisted image refinement help explore planting, materials, and the atmosphere of outdoor spaces.

Landscape design direction and planting plans: The Laurel Group design team. Selected internship work is shown here as visualization and process studies. Renderings are AI-assisted concepts.

02 / Site to concept

Start with
what is there.

A site image establishes the existing setting. The garden concept explores how a dining area, gravel surface, and layered planting could change the experience around it.

03 / An outdoor room

A frame for
outdoor living.

The terrace study introduces a pergola around an outdoor seating area. The visualization brings the proposed structure, planting, and furnishings into a single view for discussion.

04 / Comparing options

Make the difference
easy to see.

Two entry studies explore brick and stone porch finishes from a similar viewpoint. Comparing the images makes the material choice visible within the broader entry and planting scheme.

05 / The workflow

From a useful image
to a repeatable process.

The rendering workflow connects image preparation, compositing, refinement, and review. A plant-image catalog and written walkthroughs support consistency across those steps.

01 Prepare

Use clear site references and the design plan to establish the view and intended changes.

02 Compose & refine

Work with planting and material layers in Photoshop, then refine concept images with AI tools.

03 Review

Check the image against the supplied design information with the design team before using it to communicate a proposal.
